subject: Civil Engineering
title: The Aswan High Dam
description: A 60-second lesson on The Aswan High Dam.

hook.text: Egypt's lifeline — the Aswan High Dam tamed the Nile's annual floods and powered a nation.

buildup.text: Built with Soviet help from 1960-1970 — a rockfill embankment 364 feet tall and 2.3 miles wide.

discovery.text: Lake Nasser stores two years of Nile flow — ensuring water during droughts.

twist.text: Without annual floods, the Nile Delta lost its sediment supply — it's now sinking and eroding.

climax.text: Abu Simbel temples were cut apart and relocated — moved 200 feet up to escape the reservoir.

punchline.text: The dam saved Egypt from floods and drought — but the Nile Delta pays the price.

quiz.question: Why is the Nile Delta eroding since the Aswan High Dam was built?
options: The dam releases too much water, causing downstream flooding and erosion
The dam traps sediment that once replenished the delta during annual floods
Salt water from the Mediterranean is dissolving the delta soil

details.summary: The Aswan High Dam, completed in 1970 on the Nile River in Egypt, is a 111-meter-high rock-fill embankment dam that created Lake Nasser, one of the world's largest reservoirs. It controls the Nile's annual flood, provides irrigation water, and generates 2,100 megawatts of hydroelectric power.
details.whyItMatters: The Aswan Dam transformed Egyptian agriculture by eliminating the Nile's unpredictable floods and providing year-round irrigation, while also demonstrating the serious ecological consequences of large dams.
takeaways: Lake Nasser extends 500 kilometers into the upstream desert landscape
The dam eliminated the Nile's natural flood cycle that sustained agriculture for millennia
Sediment trapping has caused coastal erosion of the Nile Delta

faq.question: How did the Aswan Dam change Egyptian agriculture?
faq.answer: Before the dam, the Nile flooded annually, depositing fertile silt but also causing unpredictable damage. The dam provides year-round irrigation, enabling multiple crop cycles and converting 400,000 hectares from flood-irrigated to perennial irrigation.

faq.question: What environmental problems has the Aswan Dam caused?
faq.answer: The dam traps virtually all Nile sediment in Lake Nasser, depriving downstream farmland of natural fertilizer and causing the Nile Delta to erode and sink. Waterlogging and soil salinization increased in irrigated areas.
